0.label: female_figure_holding_bowl
0.description: The figure at the top of a slender shaft: a block-like headdress, breasts, and both arms curving down to hold a round, grooved object against the belly; below it the shaft becomes a stack of rings.
0.iconography: A woman presenting a bowl or calabash — the offering posture of devotees, and of the figures that top Ifá tappers and staffs. The grooved round form could also be a swollen belly: fertility.

panel.title: Modakeke staff: woman with a bowl above a ringed shaft
panel.object_type: staff or tapper (object in the round)
panel.summary: A slender carved shaft, not a flat panel: at its top a female figure holds a round grooved bowl or belly; below, a twisted collar, a long run of close-set rings and a plain shank with one small hatched mark.

register_readings.reading: The finial figure: a woman with a bowl.
Below (undetected): a twisted collar, about twenty rings, a plain shank.

panel.composition: Vertical: one figure at the top over long bands of texture — the usual form of an Ifá tapper or ritual staff.
panel.narrative: A devotional object: a woman offering, set above a ringed grip. With the four tappers of FoA_04-5598, it belongs to the diviner's kit recorded at Modakeke. The rings could be read as a count, but the carving gives no reason to.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'. The ring stack is a possible but unsupported count.
cross_panel_links: Offering women: the nursing figure on FoA_04-5580 (#6).
uncertainties: Low-resolution print; the object held could be a bird, a fan or a child.
